title: The illustrators, iii
logline: Friday. Montreal's letter, opened last: not a drawing of the strip — a drawing of Wood, from the strip's descriptions, which never describe him. It's close. It's the first portrait of him by a stranger and the strip hides it face-down.

panels.composition: The garage. WOOD opening the Montreal envelope. BARNABY. Three drawings on the wall already.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a man opening an envelope in a garage studio with three strangers' drawings pinned on the wall, an old dog

panels.composition: The drawing: a thin man in a chore coat from behind, at a drafting table. No face — the stranger knew not to. The coat exactly right.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a stranger's ink drawing of a thin man in a canvas chore coat seen from behind at a drafting table, no face shown
image.notes: The first portrait of Wood by a reader. From behind. The stranger knew the rule.

panels.composition: Wood looking at it. A long time. The dog looking at him looking.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a man looking at a drawing of himself from behind for a long moment while an old dog watches him, no words

panels.composition: The drawing set face-down on the table. Not pinned. The three on the wall. The fourth, hidden. The strip's rule, kept by a stranger, and then by Wood.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a man laying a drawing face down on a drafting table beneath a wall with three pinned drawings, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Montreal drew him from behind. Face down, unpinned.
